To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
algorithmic confounding increases homogeneity and reduces utility in recommendation systems.

using data from users who are already exposed to algorithmically generated recommendations creates a feedback loop that homogenizes user behaviors and leads to a decrease in the utility of the system.

(i) using data that is confounded by algorithmic recommendations increases homogeneity in users' consumption, (ii) this homogeneity can increase utility, but (iii) this utility increase is not as large as that of a non-confounded system.
